summary.text: An enantiomer is one of a pair of molecular entities that are mirror images of each other and cannot be superposed.
Like right and left hands, one cannot be laid onto the other, and no re-orientation or conformational change turns one into the other.
Chiral structures rotate plane-polarized light, but a mixture of equal amounts of both enantiomers does not rotate it.

facts.label: Other names
facts.value: Optical isomer, antipode, or optical antipode

facts.label: In proteins
facts.value: Only the L-isomer of alanine is incorporated

facts.label: Equal mixture
facts.value: A racemic mixture, which does not rotate light

facts.label: Citalopram versus escitalopram
facts.value: The pure enantiomer is typically dosed at half

facts.label: Propoxyphene pair
facts.value: One partner is an analgesic, the other an antitussive

items.prompt: A friend says you can match a molecule to its mirror image just by turning it around. Why is that wrong for enantiomers?

options.label: Turning is only allowed in two dimensions
No re-orientation or change of shape converts one into the other
Mirror images always weigh differently
The two molecules have different formulas

items.explain: Enantiomers are related by chirality, and no re-orientation or conformational change converts one into its enantiomer.

items.prompt: A solution holds exactly equal amounts of a chiral molecule's two enantiomers. What does it do to plane-polarized light?

options.label: It rotates the light clockwise
It rotates the light counterclockwise
It rotates the light twice as far
It does not rotate the light

items.explain: An equal mixture of the enantiomers is a racemic mixture, which does not rotate light.

items.prompt: A sample turns the plane of polarized light clockwise. How is it described?

options.label: Dextrorotatory, written (+)
Levorotatory, written (+)
Dextrorotatory, written (−)
Levorotatory, written (−)

items.explain: Clockwise rotation is dextrorotatory, which can also be written (+).

items.prompt: A drug company replaces a 1:1 mixture of two forms with just one form of the molecule. What is the practical aim?

options.label: To make the drug cheaper to produce
To make it rotate more light
To get improved therapeutic efficacy
To make the two forms identical

items.explain: Compositions with only one enantiomer have improved therapeutic efficacy, which is why a switch from a racemic drug is made.

items.prompt: Alanine can exist as two mirror-image forms. Which does the body build into proteins?

options.label: Only the L-isomer
Equal amounts of both
Only the D-isomer
Neither one

items.explain: In nature most chiral compounds are present as one enantiomer; only the L-isomer of alanine goes into proteins.

items.prompt: Meso tartaric acid has two asymmetric carbon atoms yet shows no enantiomerism. What explains this?

options.label: Its carbon atoms are not asymmetric
It rotates light twice as much as other forms
It contains only one kind of atom
It has a mirror symmetry plane

items.explain: A mirror symmetry plane means it does not exhibit enantiomerism despite its two asymmetric carbons.
